# ARC-1 documentation

> Use the documentation from the source revision used to build the deployed artifact.
> The website and raw source below follow main and may describe unreleased changes.

## Security review

- [Security Review](https://docs.arc-1-mcp.com/security/): where data goes, whose permissions apply, what the customer decides, and a copyable decision record.
- [Hardening Guide](https://docs.arc-1-mcp.com/security-guide/): operator configuration, dependency and release verification, and incident response.

## SAP BTP setup and administration

- [BTP Start Here](https://docs.arc-1-mcp.com/btp-overview/): choose the topology, then follow its deployment or administration links.
- [Restrict system and client access](https://docs.arc-1-mcp.com/multi-target-authorization/): optional per-user target filtering, especially for many systems/different teams. Uses IAM assignments, not automatic SAP-account discovery. Start with static roles; no IAS change required. Verify enforcement before assigning restricted users. Local path: docs_page/multi-target-authorization.md.

In a local checkout, read docs_page/btp-overview.md instead. Without a checkout, the
[raw Markdown on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arc-mcp/arc-1/main/docs_page/btp-overview.md)
is also available.

Use the same revision for linked guides and examples. Research and plans are not shipped settings.
Use docs_page/btp-setup-worksheet.md for missing inputs, owner handoffs and stop conditions.
Ask for missing landscape inputs, not passwords, tokens, private keys or raw service bindings.
Standard access is supported: its exact configuration value is standard (or leave it unset).
Target-filtered access uses xsuaa-attribute. These are the only two accepted values. Do not enable filtering just
because the installation is being upgraded. Admin diagnostics are not target execution grants;
SAPTargets is absent for ordinary readers with zero/one granted active targets in filtered mode.
